RECAP — two weeks to catch up (the 11/17 Tuesday run never fired):
WEEK 10: Lost 109.78-132.94 to christinuhh ("Little engine that kicks"). Record fell to 4-6. Lesson: Brenton Strange (8.9 on the bench) outscored started TE Hunter Henry (4.2) by 4.7, and Dylan Sampson (7.7, bench) beat started RB-flex Audric Estime (2.1) by 5.6 — two slot-for-slot misses in the same week. Both are moot now (Strange starts, Henry's benched) but it's exactly why a Thursday/Friday lineup re-check matters.
WEEK 11: Lost 90.68-152.06 to DCnutzzz ("Emeka Eggbucock"). Record fell to 4-7. Nothing was actually mismanaged — bench WR Malik Washington's 7.1 barely beat started flex Adonai Mitchell's 5.0, and bench QB Fernando Mendoza's huge 23.88 was stranded behind Shough with no second QB slot to use it. Eggbucock just had a monster week. The real story: the 6th and final playoff spot sits at 6-5, two games ahead of you, with weeks 12-14 left before the Week 15 cutoff. This is a must-win stretch, not a rebuilding one.

Everyone else is clean: Chase Brown and Tee Higgins get the week's best matchup on your roster (27.5 implied vs. New Orleans), Zay Flowers draws the league's #1-graded defense (Houston) but still has a real floor, Bryant and Mitchell are low-ceiling flex plays with no better bench option, and Aubrey gets the Thanksgiving dome showcase game (49.5 total).
Waivers / trades: see the Waivers tab (Rodriguez Jr. + a TE add) and Trades tab (a real, evidence-based TE upgrade idea this week).

SLEEPER — New idea this week, and it's grounded in actual roster data: efrain115 (8-3, in the thick of the 1-seed race) is carrying THREE tight ends — starter Isaiah Likely, plus Mike Gesicki and T.J. Hockenson both stuck on the bench. Offer Jordan Watkins (WR, SF) + Dylan Sampson (RB, CLE) — two pure bench fliers you aren't starting and wouldn't miss — for Mike Gesicki. It fixes your single biggest roster weakness (TE) without touching a single one of your current starters, and hands them two depth pieces for a TE3 they have no use for. Checked against weeks 15-17 first: this makes you stronger, not weaker, since Gesicki unseats nothing you currently start — exactly the kind of move that's fine to make even while you're fighting for a playoff spot. Separate note, not pursued: JonnyClips (8-3, 1st place) is also sitting on a Brock Bowers/Mark Andrews TE surplus, but Bowers is currently tagged "Out" and the gap between what a 1st-place, fully-stacked roster would want back and what you can offer without touching a starter is too wide for a realistic one-sided ask this week — Gesicki is the more realistic shot.

Tempting as that pattern looks, don't chase last week's points by benching your clearly better asset — that exact overcorrection sat live in your Week 4 lineup for five straight days (Shough over Herbert) until this run flagged it again.

Left the QB slot completely empty all week (Shough would've scored 15.94 sitting there unused) and started Josh Downs (4.6) over Omarion Hampton (13.3) in the flex — an 8.7-point unforced error stacked on a totally wasted roster slot. A win over a weak opponent papered over the worst bench-management week of the season so far; double-check every single slot is filled before Thursday lock, every week, no exceptions.

Nothing was mismanaged this week (Herbert/Tuten/Brown/Higgins/Wilson/Strange/Downs/Flowers/Aubrey/Jaguars was the right call going in) — Weak Homie Quon just had a bigger week. Separately, Jaguars DEF cratered to 2.0 for the second time in three weeks despite a plus matchup grade — stop trusting the defRank alone for that unit, check the actual opposing offense's health too.

Don't chase last week's box score without checking the bye schedule first.

Bench K Brandon Aubrey (14.0) outscored started Jason Myers (8.0) by 6.0 — the week's only avoidable miss; Tuten and Hampton both being on bye forced the rest of the lineup, no mistake there. The bigger story heading into Week 8: Tyler Shough is your ONLY rostered QB, and New Orleans' bye lands this week — a zero-QB-depth problem that's been sitting unnoticed on this roster all season and is now live. Fix it on waivers, and keep a real backup QB rostered going forward so a single bye week doesn't cost you a start.

Zay Flowers' 0.0 is now explained and wasn't a bad call — Lamar Jackson left the Bills game on the first series with a thumb injury (surgery, IR-bound) and Baltimore's backup QB play sank the whole passing game; nothing to have flagged going in.
